## FINAL RESULT (approved scheme)

**Pearson correlation between gene length and gene expression, protein-coding genes only:**
**r = 0.4219  (p < 1×10⁻³⁰⁰, effectively 0; n = 19,942)**

Exact calculation (as approved):
- filter: `gene_biotype == 'protein_coding'` → **19,942 genes** (multi-locus collapsed rows excluded);
- `E_g` = mean of batch-corrected read count over **all 723 samples**;
- `x = log2(E_g + 1)`, `y = log10(Length)`;
- `scipy.stats.pearsonr(x, y)` → **r = 0.421946**, t = 65.7, p underflows double precision (stored 0.0; report as p < 1e-300). Positive and highly significant: longer protein-coding genes are modestly more highly expressed in these blood immune-cell samples.

## SENSITIVITY TABLE (Pearson r, n = 19,942)

| Definition (x vs y) | r |
|---|---|
| raw mean count vs raw Length (bp) | 0.0504 |
| raw mean count vs log10(Length) | 0.0477 |
| log2(E+1) vs raw Length | 0.3204 |
| **log2(E+1) vs log10(Length) — PRIMARY** | **0.4219** |
| mean-of-log2(count+1) vs log10(Length) | 0.4133 |
| **mean-of-log − log-of-mean Δr** | **−0.0086** |

**Δr = −0.0086 ≤ 0.05 → discrepancy is negligible; per your instruction I simply state this:** the pooled-mean (log-of-mean, primary) and mean-of-log differ by <0.01 in r and neither is preferable on a material basis; the primary scheme (log2 of the pooled mean count) is what the question's "gene expression" most naturally denotes, and it is retained as the answer.

**Per-cell-type** (log2(mean within cell type + 1) vs log10(Length)): CD14 r = 0.375, CD19 r = 0.407, CD8 r = 0.411, CD4 r = 0.417, PBMC r = 0.424; pooled all-samples r = 0.422. All five cell types agree with the pooled value (range 0.375–0.424), so the pooled answer is not an artifact of any single cell type. The raw-vs-raw r is much lower (0.050) purely because raw counts are dominated by a few highly expressed genes; logging both variables is the appropriate Pearson setting.

## PROTEIN-CODING LENGTH DISTRIBUTION (bp)
n = 19,942; **min 51, median 4,336, mean 5,331.5, max 118,976**; Q1 = 2,487, Q3 = 6,948; 0.04% of protein-coding genes ≤100 bp; 10.9% ≥10 kb. (Length = per-gene exonic/transcript-level length in nucleotides, not full chromosome span.)
